title: Sessions are keyed by the literal cwd string, so a symlinked path splits one project's history
observed: Sessions created by 'kiln -p' launched without a shell recorded cwd /private/tmp/…/proj (Go's os.Getwd resolving /tmp's symlink when PWD is stale); an interactive launch after 'cd /tmp/…/proj' records /tmp/…/proj and lists no recent sessions — the session lookup matches Cwd by exact string (internal/session/jsonl/repo.go).
expected: The same directory is one project however it was reached: compare cwd after filepath.EvalSymlinks (and store the resolved path), so --continue and Recent sessions find sessions started via either spelling.
